bifrost: springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs (pairing and device state), springboard/src/shell/pages.rs (Bluetooth Settings page)
summary: BifrOSt pairs, connects and forgets Bluetooth devices from the Settings Bluetooth page, using a Just Works pairing flow with no passkey or confirmation UI. None of Apple's reusable Bluetooth controllers (pairing panel, device selector, service browser, object push, passkey display) exist as an app-facing SDK API.

features.note: Pairing works only as a Settings list action. No modal panel, no title or prompt customisation, no UUID filter, and no SDK API. Pairing always uses NoInputNoOutput (Just Works), so the user's tap is the only consent.

features.note: Wave 5 (theme-09, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The kernel's user-confirm request is auto-answered: confirm if the address matches the pairing we started, otherwise negative reply. The passkey is never shown to the user, so the user cannot compare or type one.

No Bluetooth picker UI exists in the SDK, and the accessibility element map (ui/src/ax.rs) has no ignored-element flag, so no cell can be hidden from assistive technology. The accessibility bridge exists for the shell, but nothing marks Bluetooth-specific cells as ignored.

gaps: No app-facing SDK API for Bluetooth pairing, device choice or status: the pairing and device list live only in the Settings Bluetooth page (springboard/src/shell/pages.rs).
No reusable device selector sheet or panel (IOBluetoothDeviceSelectorController).
No passkey or numeric comparison pairing: pairing is hardwired to NoInputNoOutput (springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs:68-69), so devices that need a PIN or passkey cannot pair.
No SDP service browser: no service list or UUID-filtered selection (IOBluetoothServiceBrowserController).
No Bluetooth object push or file transfer (IOBluetoothObjectPushUIController). springboard/src/net/share.rs covers LAN sharing only.
No UUID filter for pairing (addAllowedUUID and clearAllowedUUIDs).
The Apple reference types (BluetoothKeyboardReturnType, the IOBluetoothUI constants and functions) have no BifrOSt counterpart.
